note: This is a hand-curated copy of the SlopLens rule catalog, adapted for a static source scan. SlopLens owns the rule identity, name, category, family, supporting flag and fix line. Everything specific to a source scan is owned here: the staticPlain wording, the observation and inference split, the assessment, the file types and the thresholds. There are no weights and no score, because a repository is not a page. Run the drift check in the Slop Detector repository after changing either copy.
limitations: This scan reads source files. It cannot see the rendered page, so checks that need layout, computed styles or the accessibility tree are reported as unassessed rather than guessed.
It cannot tell who or what wrote the code, and it does not try.
A finding is a candidate for review, not a verdict. No single finding decides quality on its own.

rules.name: Buzzword copy
rules.fix: Say what the product actually does, who it helps, and what changes for them.
rules.staticPlain: Headings, buttons and short blurbs in the source lean on stock marketing phrases that could describe almost any product. A single phrase counts for little, and more only add up when they make a real share of the short copy. Long-form prose is left out.
rules.observation: String literals and template text used as headings, buttons, link labels or short blurbs, matched against the stock phrase list.
rules.inference: The wording is generic. It does not show that the words reached the interface, or that the product lacks substance elsewhere.

rules.name: Em dash overload
rules.fix: Rewrite a few of those sentences with commas, periods or parentheses.
rules.staticPlain: Em dashes turn up in a noticeable share of the headings, buttons and short blurbs, a punctuation habit of stock marketing copy. Quotations, their sources, number ranges and long-form prose are left out.
rules.observation: Short copy strings containing an em dash, excluding a dash that opens a line and a dash between two digits.
rules.inference: The punctuation is used as a style habit in short copy. Long-form prose and quoted material are not judged.

rules.name: Bold label in every bullet
rules.fix: Write some points as sentences and let the important words stand out on their own.
rules.staticPlain: Most bullets in one list open with a short bold label and a colon. It looks organised without organising anything, because every point gets the same mechanical shape.
rules.observation: List items whose text opens with a short bold label and a colon.
rules.inference: The shape is present in source. Which items render together in one list is not shown by source alone.
rules.unassessedReason: Planned, not yet checked. Grouping bullets into the list a reader actually sees needs a rendered view, so the source scan does not attempt it yet.

rules.name: Clipped slogans
rules.fix: Write the idea as one connected sentence that says what the product or person actually does.
rules.staticPlain: Short lines in the copy are built from two or more clipped fragments of one to three words each, a rhythm that stock copy uses in place of saying something.
rules.observation: Copy strings made only of short capitalised fragments, each ending in a period.
rules.inference: This is a rendered measure.
rules.unassessedReason: Planned, not yet checked. SlopLens measures this on rendered text; a source pattern for it has not been written or calibrated yet.

rules.name: Gradient headline text
rules.fix: Use one solid, high-contrast color and let the words carry the emphasis.
rules.staticPlain: Text filled with a color gradient is a strong template tell, especially in headlines.
rules.observation: A declaration that clips the background to text together with a gradient background in the same rule, or a class string combining a text-clip utility with a gradient utility.
rules.inference: The technique is present in the source. Whether the gradient is visible, and whether the element is a headline, is not judged.

rules.name: Accent word in the headline
rules.fix: Set the heading in one color and style, and let the words themselves carry the emphasis.
rules.staticPlain: One word or short phrase inside a heading is set in a different color or in italic, a highlight habit that template headlines repeat.
rules.observation: The rendered color and font style of a short run inside a heading, compared with the heading itself.
rules.inference: This is a rendered measure.
rules.unassessedReason: Planned, not yet checked. It needs the computed color and style of text inside a heading, which source alone does not show.

rules.name: Glow, blur and gradients
rules.fix: Keep the effects that explain depth or hierarchy and drop the ones that are only decoration.
rules.staticPlain: Colorful gradients, frosted glass and big glowing shadows appear across several separate files. Effects inside one illustration or one component count once.
rules.observation: A colorful gradient, a saturated glow of at least 24 pixels, or a backdrop blur, counted per file including their utility-class equivalents.
rules.inference: The effects are declared. The rendered page may place them all in one illustration, which would count once.

rules.name: Emoji as decoration
rules.fix: Use a consistent icon set, or let plain text stand on its own.
rules.staticPlain: Emoji are doing the job of icons or bullet points in headings, lists and buttons. Plain copyright, registered and trademark signs are not emoji and are left out.
rules.observation: Emoji-presentation characters inside heading, list item or button text, needing at least two matches in a file.
rules.inference: Emoji appear in interface copy. Whether they were meant as decoration or as content is not judged.

rules.name: Arrow on every link
rules.fix: Let clear link text do the work and keep arrows for real direction.
rules.staticPlain: Many links end with the same decorative arrow.
rules.observation: Anchor text ending with an arrow character, needing at least three matches and at least 15 per cent of the file's links.
rules.inference: The arrow is repeated in the source. It does not show how the links look or whether the arrow carries meaning.

rules.name: Boxes inside boxes
rules.fix: Use spacing or a divider for inner groups and keep one container per region.
rules.staticPlain: Content sits inside several rounded, bordered boxes stacked into each other.
rules.observation: The rendered nesting depth, corner radius and border of real elements.
rules.inference: This is a rendered measure, so source alone cannot support it.
rules.unassessedReason: Needs the rendered page. Nesting depth, radius and border are computed from real elements, which a source scan does not have.

rules.name: Mixed icon styles
rules.fix: Pick one icon style per group so equal actions look equal.
rules.staticPlain: Small interface icons in the same group mix outlined and filled styles. Logos and illustrations are left out.
rules.observation: Two different icon libraries imported, or both outline and solid variants of one library used in the same file.
rules.inference: Both styles are present in the file. Whether they appear together in one group of controls is not judged.

rules.name: Cookie-cutter feature cards
rules.fix: Give the most important point more room, or show the product doing the thing instead of describing it.
rules.staticPlain: A row of identical cards, each with a small icon, a heading and a blurb, is the most familiar block in template land. Rows whose cards each lead to their own page or carry concrete detail count lightly.
rules.observation: Repeated sibling cards in a rendered row, and whether each card leads somewhere or carries detail.
rules.inference: This is a rendered measure. In source, a card row is one template inside a loop, so the count and the repetition are not visible.
rules.unassessedReason: Needs the rendered page. A source card row is a single template inside a loop, so source cannot show how many cards render or whether they repeat.

rules.name: Same section, again
rules.fix: Shape each section around its own content instead of reusing one layout.
rules.staticPlain: Several sections share exactly the same structure, so the page feels assembled from one block.
rules.observation: How many rendered sections share one structural signature.
rules.inference: This is a rendered measure. Source components do not show how often each is used on a page.
rules.unassessedReason: Needs the rendered page. Repeated sections are counted from the document, and source components do not show their usage.

rules.name: Stock hero layout
rules.fix: Open with something specific to this product, such as the product itself or a concrete result.
rules.staticPlain: The opening screen is a centered headline over one filled and one plain button, the default hero in nearly every starter kit.
rules.observation: The rendered position and fill of the headline and its button pair.
rules.inference: This is a rendered measure. Centering, button fill and button placement are all geometry.
rules.unassessedReason: Needs the rendered page. The hero shape is measured from centering, button fill and button position.

rules.name: Pill badge over the headline
rules.fix: Fold real news into the page itself, or drop the badge if there is nothing new to announce.
rules.staticPlain: A small rounded announcement badge sits above the main headline, a fixture of template landing pages.
rules.observation: The rendered position, height and corner radius of a small element above the headline.
rules.inference: This is a rendered measure.
rules.unassessedReason: Needs the rendered page. The badge is identified by its rendered position, height and corner radius above the headline.

rules.name: Numbered labels on everything
rules.fix: Drop the numbers unless the order matters, and let the headings name the items.
rules.staticPlain: Three or more labels open with zero-padded numbers such as 01, 02 and 03 on items that are not steps.
rules.observation: Visible labels that open with zero-padded numbers, outside ordered lists, tables and steps.
rules.inference: This is a rendered measure.
rules.unassessedReason: Planned, not yet checked. SlopLens measures this on rendered labels; a source pattern for it has not been written or calibrated yet.

rules.name: Leftover template text
rules.fix: Replace every placeholder and prompt leftover with real content, and point each link at a real page.
rules.staticPlain: Placeholder words, prompt leftovers or chat replies were left in, which usually means a template was shipped before it was finished. Four or more links that go nowhere count lightly on their own.
rules.observation: Placeholder and machine-residue patterns in short copy, plus anchors whose target is only a hash and whose label carries no number.
rules.inference: Placeholder content is present in the source. Whether that string is ever rendered is not judged.

rules.name: Placeholder testimonial company
rules.fix: Replace it with a testimonial from someone readers can find, or remove the quote.
rules.staticPlain: A customer quote credits a company name that reads as a placeholder, such as TechCorp, Acme Inc or Lorem Ipsum. This is the strongest form of invented proof, and a real quote from a person readers can look up does not count.
rules.observation: A placeholder company name inside the attribution line of a quotation or a figure caption.
rules.inference: The attribution reads as a placeholder. A real company that happens to share the name would also match.

rules.name: Numbers without a source
rules.fix: Publish one real figure with its method and a link, or remove the claim until you can.
rules.staticPlain: Customer counts, speed multipliers and percentage claims sit in the copy with no source, link or method beside them. A number nobody can check is a landing-page habit rather than evidence.
rules.observation: A claim pattern in a short block that contains no link and no source word, outside navigation, footers, articles, tables and quotations.
rules.inference: A claim is present and its source is not in the same file. The source may live in a sibling component, a prop or a footnote, so this is a candidate for review rather than a verdict.

rules.name: Kit default colors
rules.fix: Choose accent colors for this brand rather than accepting the kit defaults.
rules.staticPlain: The accent colors are the untouched defaults of a UI kit such as Tailwind, Bootstrap or Material, which only counts when other slop signals are present.
rules.observation: Utility classes or color values matching a kit accent palette, used at least three times in one file.
rules.inference: A kit color is used. The theme may override it, so an untouched accent is not established. When a Tailwind 3 configuration sets its own colors, this rule is left unassessed rather than guessed.

rules.name: Stock icon set
rules.fix: Draw a few key icons for the product, or use fewer icons and let the words carry the meaning.
rules.staticPlain: The icons come straight from a popular free icon set, which only counts when other slop signals are present.
rules.observation: An import from a known icon package, or at least four icon components used from one package in a file.
rules.inference: The icon set is a stock library. A stock icon set is a normal choice and is not evidence of poor quality on its own.

rules.name: Endless scroll
rules.fix: Cut sections that repeat a point and give the remaining ones more substance.
rules.staticPlain: The page runs well past six laptop screens, the stacked-section length of a typical template, which only counts when other slop signals are present.
rules.observation: The rendered document height in laptop screens.
rules.inference: This is a rendered measure.
rules.unassessedReason: Needs the rendered page. Page length is measured from the document height, which a source scan does not have.

rules.name: Label above every heading
rules.fix: Work the useful words into the heading, or drop the label where it adds nothing.
rules.staticPlain: A small label sits above section headings in several separate sections, usually in capitals or wide letter spacing and often repeating the heading in fewer words. Plenty of editorial layouts use one label now and then, so this only counts when other slop signals are present.
rules.observation: The rendered position, size and letter spacing of a small label above a section heading.
rules.inference: This is a rendered measure.
rules.unassessedReason: Planned, not yet checked. It needs the rendered position of a small label above a heading, which source alone does not show.

rules.name: Dotted metadata strings
rules.fix: Keep the facts readers need and write them as a sentence or a proper list.
rules.staticPlain: Several short lines string three or more fragments together with middle dots as decoration rather than information. This only counts when other slop signals are present.
rules.observation: Short rendered lines that join three or more fragments with middle dots, outside navigation and footers.
rules.inference: This is a rendered measure.
rules.unassessedReason: Planned, not yet checked. SlopLens measures this on rendered text; a source pattern for it has not been written or calibrated yet.

rules.name: Underlined links
rules.fix: Mark links through clear labels, placement, color and a visible focus outline instead of underlines.
rules.staticPlain: A real share of the links are underlined at rest, or carry an underline that slides in on hover. Underlines are a common accessibility choice, so this only counts when other slop signals are present.
rules.observation: The rendered text decoration, bottom border, pseudo-element bar or gradient stripe on links.
rules.inference: This is a rendered measure.
rules.unassessedReason: Planned, not yet checked. It needs the computed styles of links and their pseudo-elements, which source alone does not show.

rules.name: Spills off phones
rules.fix: Let the element wrap or shrink to fit its container on small screens.
rules.staticPlain: Some content runs past the edge of a phone screen.
rules.observation: The rendered position of elements against a phone-width viewport.
rules.inference: This is a rendered measure.
rules.unassessedReason: Needs the rendered page. Overflow is measured at phone width, which a source scan does not have.

rules.name: Unlabeled buttons
rules.fix: Give every control a visible label or an accessible name.
rules.staticPlain: Some buttons, links or fields have no accessible name, so screen readers cannot announce them.
rules.observation: A button or link whose only child is an icon or an image with no alt text, and that has no aria-label, aria-labelledby or title, or an input with no label.
rules.inference: No name is visible in the source. A name added at runtime, or a wrapper component's own labelling, would not be seen.

rules.name: Invisible keyboard focus
rules.fix: Add a clear focus outline to links and buttons.
rules.staticPlain: Pressing Tab moves focus, but nothing on screen shows where it went.
rules.observation: A rule or class string that removes the outline with no focus-visible replacement in the same rule or class string.
rules.inference: The outline is removed in one place. A replacement may exist in a global stylesheet or another rule, so this is a candidate for review.

rules.name: Uneven buttons
rules.fix: Use one shared size for equivalent buttons.
rules.staticPlain: Buttons that do similar jobs come in noticeably different heights.
rules.observation: The rendered heights of buttons in one group.
rules.inference: This is a rendered measure.
rules.unassessedReason: Needs the rendered page. Button height is a rendered measure.

rules.name: Uneven padding
rules.fix: Share one padding value between equivalent controls.
rules.staticPlain: Similar buttons use noticeably different inner padding.
rules.observation: The rendered padding of buttons in one group.
rules.inference: This is a rendered measure.
rules.unassessedReason: Needs the rendered page. Button padding is a rendered measure.

rules.name: Ignores reduced motion
rules.fix: Pause non-essential animation under the reduced-motion setting.
rules.staticPlain: Animations keep running even when someone asks their device for less motion.
rules.observation: A keyframe animation, an infinite animation or an animate utility in a package that carries no reduced-motion guard anywhere.
rules.inference: No guard was found in the package. A guard may be applied globally or at runtime, so this is a candidate for review.

rules.name: Images without alt text
rules.fix: Describe each content image in its alt attribute, and use an empty alt only for decoration.
rules.staticPlain: Some content images have no alt attribute at all, so screen readers skip them and a broken image goes unnoticed. Images marked as decorative with an empty alt are left out.
rules.observation: An image element written literally with no alt attribute and no spread props.
rules.inference: The attribute is absent in the source. A spread or a wrapper component would hide it, so those are skipped rather than reported.

rules.name: Broken or empty image
rules.fix: Add the intended image and check that it loads, or remove the image.
rules.staticPlain: Some images point at a file that is missing or was never set, so the page shows a broken icon or an empty space where the picture should be.
rules.observation: An image source that is empty, or a literal relative or root-absolute path that does not exist in the nearest package's public directory, checked case-exactly.
rules.inference: The file is missing on this machine. A build step, a different deploy root or a case difference would change the result.

rules.name: Mouse-only controls
rules.fix: Use a button or a link, or give the box a button role and a tab stop with keyboard handling.
rules.staticPlain: Some things act like buttons or links but are boxes with a click handler, so a keyboard cannot reach or press them. Real buttons, links with an address and boxes with a tab stop are left out.
rules.observation: A click handler on a div or span with no role, no tab stop and no inner interactive control.
rules.inference: The box is clickable and unreachable in the source. Keyboard activation and event bubbling are not proven.

rules.name: Skipped heading levels
rules.fix: Step down one heading level at a time so the outline matches the content.
rules.staticPlain: Heading levels skip on the way down, such as a second-level heading followed by a fourth-level one, which makes the page outline harder to follow with a screen reader.
rules.observation: Within one complete document, a heading whose level is more than one below the previous heading.
rules.inference: The jump is in source order within one file. Across components the rendered order may differ, so only complete documents are checked.
